minutes_text:
MINUTES
  PARKS AND RECREATION COMMISSION
  REGULAR MEETING
  MARCH 17, 2026
  MULTIPURPOSE ROOM
  6:30 P.M.

MEETING CALL TO ORDER

  Chair Villablanca called the meeting to order at 6:30 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Chair Judy Villablanca; Vice Chair Jake Lingo; and Commissioners Georgia
  Goldfarb and Dane Skophammer

  ABSENT: Commissioner Alicia Peak

  ALSO PRESENT: Kate Manisco, Community Services Deputy Director; Chris Orosz,
  Recreation Manager; Brittany Saleaumua, Administrative Assistant; Joie Cosentino,
  Recreation Coordinator; and Raphael Winkler, Part-Time Permanent Recreation Assistant
  II

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Chair Villablanca led the Pledge of Allegiance.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Commissioner Goldfarb moved, and Vice Chair Lingo seconded a motion to
  approve the agenda. The question was called, and the motion carried 4—0;
  Commissioner Peak absent.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Administrative Assistant Saleaumua reported that the agenda for the meeting was
  posted on March 11, 2026.

ITEM 1  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS

  A.  Election of Chair and Vice Chair

  Chair Villablanca stated that the election of Chair and Vice Chair would be
  postponed to the next Regular meeting, as Commissioner Peak was absent.

  Senior Center Program Presentation by Recreation Coordinator Joie Cosentino

  Deputy Director Manisco introduced Recreation Coordinator Joie Cosentino and
  Part—Time Permanent Recreation Assistant II Raphael Winkler. She stated both
  employees worked at the Senior Center at Malibu City Hall.

  Recreation Coordinator Cosentino gave updates on the operation of the Senior
  Center, including an overview of programs, excursions, events, and the Dial-A-
  Ride program.

  In response to Commissioner Skophammer, Deputy Director Manisco stated that
  the census data was pulled from 2023, but the demographic numbers are projected
  for each year.

  In response to Commissioner Skophammer, Recreation Coordinator Cosentino
  stated that program offerings were based on participant feedback.

  In response to Commissioner Goldfarb, Recreation Coordinator Cosentino stated
  the walking group would meet at Malibu Bluffs Park before croquet and bocce ball
  classes begin.

ITEM 2  WRITTEN AND ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FROM THE PUBLIC

  Louise Greene thanked staff for planning a bocce ball program and for extending
  the time for the senior knitting group.

  Kevin Keegan stated he wanted to discuss programming ideas for Los Angeles
  2028 Olympic and to include discussions with the Harry Barovsky Memorial Youth
  Commission.

  Haley Rivers stated she was using the Malibu Equestrian Park for horse training
  lessons and wanted to ensure it remains part of the community.

  Sanaa Pharayra wanted to maintain public access to the Malibu Equestrian Park.
  She stated the park required maintenance; however, the equestrian community was
  present in Malibu.

  Haylynn Conrad complimented Senior Center staff for their hard work and for
  listening to participant feedback.

ITEM 3  CONSENT CALENDAR

MOTION  Vice Chair Lingo moved, and Commissioner Goldfarb seconded a motion to
  approve the consent calendar. The question was called, and the motion carried 4-0;
  Commissioner Peak absent.

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following items:
  A.  Previously Discussed Items
  None.
  B.  New Items
  1.  Approval of Minutes
  Recommended Action: Approve the minutes for the December 9, 2025
  Parks and Recreation Commission Special meeting.
  2.  Community Services Department Monthly Report
  Recommended Action: Receive and flle a report of activities, events.
  proj ects, and programs coordinated by the Community Services Department
  in February 2026.

ITEM 4  OLD BUSINESS

  None.

ITEM 5  NEW BUSINESS

  Earth Friendly Management Policy Quarterly Update
  Recommended Action: Receive and file a report on the Earth Friendly Management
  Policy activities from July 2025 through December 2025.

  Recreation Manager Orosz presented the staff report.

  Commissioner Skophammer stated the City should be recognized for its
  participation and commitment to the Monarch Pledge.

  In response to Vice Chair Lingo, Recreation Manager Orosz stated gopher
  mitigation solutions would require a discussion with the parks division. He stated
  the reintroduction of gopher snakes could be done at Legacy Park.

  In response to Chair Villablanca, Recreation Manager Orosz stated that a permit
  from the State would be required to move a native species from one parcel to
  another.

  In response to Commissioner Skophammer, Recreation Manager Orosz stated that
  the Pepperdine University study was proposed because the students were seeking a
  solution to a problem already present.

  Commissioner Skophammer suggested applying for the special permit while the
  study was underway rather than waiting until it was completed.

  Commissioner Goldfarb suggested new invasive species signage for public
  education.

  Las Flores Creek Park Playground Replacement Proiect
  Recommended Action: Review and provide feedback on the Las Flores Creek Park
  playground design.

  Community Services Deputy Director Manisco presented the staff report.

  Scott Dittrich supported a new dog park at Las Flores Creek Park. He stated the
  playground was underutilized and suggested the Commission research park use and
  amenities before installing a new playground.

  Commissioner Goldfarb stated the old playground equipment was splintered and
  hoped the new equipment did not have that issue.

  In response to Commissioner Goldfarb, Community Services Deputy Director
  Manisco stated the rubber pour-in-place surface was required and made from
  recyclable material.

  Commissioner Skophammer stated the picnic tables were too far away from the
  playground and asked if they could be moved closer.

  In response to Commissioner Skophammer, Community Services Deputy Director
  Manisco stated the playground area could not accommodate swings due to the
  required fall zone.

  In response to Chair Villablanca, Community Services Deputy Director Manisco
  stated that the septic system was damaged during the Palisades Fire and it would
  be repaired during Phase 2 along with the playground.

MOTION  Commissioner Skophammer moved, and Chair Villablanca seconded a motion to
  approve the Las Flores Creek Park playground design. The question was called,
  and the motion carried 4-0; Commissioner Peak absent.

ITEM 6  STAFF UPDATES

  Community Services Deputy Director Manisco provided an update on the Chumash
  Day Powwow, Automated External Defibrillator (AED) installation, and the
  California Parks and Recreation Society (CPRS) 2025 Award of Excellence.

  Recreation Manager Orosz provided an update on the whale-watching telescopes
  at Malibu Bluffs Park and Outdoor Recreation programs.

  In response to Commissioner Goldfarb, Recreation Manager Orosz stated he would
  research the feasibility to install a telescope at a Charmlee Wildemess Park
  overlook.

  Community Services Deputy Director Manisco provided an update on the Skate
  Park and Snack Shack.

ITEM 7  COMMISSIONER REPORTS, COMMENTS AND INQUIRIES

  Vice Chair Lingo stated that Malibu Little League's Opening Day was successful
  and a theft occurred at the snack shack.

  Chair Villablanca stated she would attend the Chumash Day Powwow and inquired
  about bikes at the Skate Park. She stated she provided Council with a Commission
  update and inquired if the Commission could have ajoint meeting with the Harry
  Barovsky Memorial Youth Commission.

FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  None.

ADJOURNMENT

  Commissioner Skophammer adjourned the meeting at 8:03 p.m.
